# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Mute. My manual says: cut the yellow wire, press the key wearing 2, cut the orange wire, press the key wearing 7 — in that order only. My one outgoing channel is gestures, and only Deaf receives them; Deaf cannot hear a word I would "say," so no code exists between us yet. Deaf can, however, speak, and I can hear — so Deaf can propose meanings aloud and I can answer with gestures.

My best opening is iconic material Deaf can hook onto what is printed on the bomb: ✌ reads naturally as "two," and 🖐 followed by ✌ reads as five-and-two, i.e. seven. If the keys on this bomb wear 2 and 7, Deaf may connect my numbers to those keys, and the order I send them in (2 first, 7 second) hints at the order of the key presses. I close with 👍👎, which I intend as a yes/no channel — the tool we will need to negotiate everything else, including which wire is which, once Deaf describes the bomb's layout and I can point. Nobody should cut or press anything until the full four-step sequence has been confirmed with me.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🖐", "✌", "👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Hands report, for the one who reads the manual. In the order my hands meet the casing: a display whose text I cannot read by touch; a small light, colour unknown to me; a strip with three engraved marks, the first two identical, like a spiral coiled inside a circle, the third different, like a crooked X or a bird's footprint; a keypad of four keys that wants 2 digits and has nothing entered yet; and a row of six wires I can cut. The keypad keys, in my slot order 1 to 4, read: 2, 3, 7, 1. I number the wires 1 to 6 along the row; my numbering may be mirrored from the deaf one's view, but the deaf one can see my hands, so we can calibrate before any cut. I never see gestures, and I will never hear you, since you cannot speak. The only road from your manual to my hands runs through the deaf one's voice: find the rules for the display, the light, the strip marks, the keypad and the wires, and sign them to the deaf one so the deaf one can speak me each instruction step by step. I will touch nothing until told.
Deaf says: Everyone — the full bomb, in words. The display shows the number six. There is a light and it is lit green. A painted strip shows three colours in this order: red, blue, yellow. The keypad has four buttons; in a row from the left their printed labels are two, three, seven, one. It wants a two-digit code and nothing has been entered yet. Six wires run left to right: one orange, two yellow, three blue, four red, five white, six green. That is everything I can see.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — you cannot speak and I am the only one who sees your hands, so I will relay everything to Blind by voice. Let's fix a code now. Numbers by fingers: ☝ is one, ✌ is two, 👌 is three, 🤟 is four, 🖐 is five, 🤙 is six, ✊ is zero, 🤞 is seven. The bomb's parts, numbered: ☝ display, ✌ light, 👌 strip, 🤟 keypad, 🖐 wires. I just spoke the bomb's whole description to both of you, so match your manual to it. For wires, send six thumbs in a row, 👍 cut, 👎 keep, left to right. For the keypad, send the two code digits as number hands. 👍 is yes, 👎 is no, 👋 means say that again. Your first message to me read as two, five, two, thumbs-up, thumbs-down — what did you mean? If it was about wires, resend it in the six-thumb format. Start with whatever module the manual says must be dealt with first.

Deaf's description matches my manual perfectly. The manual demands exactly four steps: cut the yellow wire, press the key wearing 2, cut the orange wire, press the key wearing 7 — nothing else. On the bomb, only wire 2 (Deaf's left-to-right) is yellow and only wire 1 is orange, so the wire targets are unambiguous; the keypad wears a 2 and a 7, so the code digits are 2 then 7, entered in the manual's interleaved order. My first garbled message was an early attempt at "2 then 7" — Deaf's new number code makes that obsolete, and I'll now speak entirely in the code Deaf proposed, which I adopt by using it.

I'm sending the whole sequence in one message, with Deaf's module markers so the boundaries are clear: display 👎, light 👎, strip 👎 (none of them appear in my manual — nothing to do there, leave them), then wires 👎👍👎👎👎👎 (cut only the second-from-left, the yellow), then keypad ✌, then wires 👍👎👎👎👎👎 (cut only the first, the orange), then keypad 🤞. I am deliberately not certifying anything with 👍 yet: Deaf must relay the yellow-wire cut first, resolve the mirroring between Blind's numbering and Deaf's left-right view — Deaf can see Blind's hands and calibrate — and echo the plan back. Only when Deaf reads it back correctly will I answer 👍 and let Blind's hands move.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👎", "✌", "👎", "👌", "👎", "🖐", "👎", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "🤟", "✌", "🖐", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "🤟", "🤞"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, full merged picture for your manual. Calibration confirmed: the deaf one read the keypad left to right as two three seven one, exactly my slot order, so my wire positions one to six are the deaf one's left to right: one orange, two yellow, three blue, four red, five white, six green. Phrase rules by colour and digit value where the manual allows; colour is mirror-proof, though orientation is already confirmed. The complete bomb as we jointly perceive it: the display shows the digit six, and I cannot read it by touch, so if it ever changes the deaf one must re-read it to me. The light is lit, green. The strip has three engraved marks: positions one and two are the same shape, a spiral coiled in a circle; position three is different, a crooked claw or bird's footprint. Painted colours left to right: red, blue, yellow. Mind the trap: the two identical shapes carry different colours, so check whether the manual keys on shape or on colour. The keypad wants a two-digit code, nothing entered; slot one prints two, slot two three, slot three seven, slot four one. The wires I cut by position one to six, colours as listed. Your road to me runs through the deaf one's voice, so here is a code you and the deaf one can both use with no negotiation: number the gesture alphabet one to forty-two in its printed order. Positions one to nine mean the digits one to nine; position ten means zero; positions eleven to thirty-six mean the letters A to Z in order; position thirty-seven is a space. So the third gesture in the printed list means three, the eleventh means A. If you and the deaf one already settled a workable code, keep yours; I never see gestures, I only need the deaf one's spoken result. But if nothing is settled, use this: the deaf one already proposed a number code, and the deaf one can check any decoded rule against the real bomb as an error check. What I need back, in the deaf one's spoken words: what the lit green light demands, what the display's six means, what the strip requires, the two-digit keypad code, and any wire instructions, with cut and press orders as explicit numbers. I am holding my hands: nothing pressed, nothing cut, until rules arrive.
Blind gestures: [👍 🤙 ✋]
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — I decoded your message this far: display no, light no, strip no; then wires, reading as keep, cut, keep, keep, keep, keep, meaning cut wire 2, yellow; then keypad with digits 2 and 5; then another six thumbs, cut wire 1, orange; then digits 4 and 7. Problem: the keypad has no button labeled 5 — its labels are only 2, 3, 7, 1 — so 2 and 5 cannot be pressed as printed numbers. Answer me with a run of 👍 and 👎 in this exact order, one sign each. One: is the first action a keypad entry? Two: is an early action cutting the yellow wire, number 2? Three: is an early action cutting the orange wire, number 1? Four: do the two wire instructions come in sequence, yellow first, orange later? Five: are 2 and 5 button positions rather than printed labels? Six: what must actually be entered on the keypad — send exactly two of your number signs drawn from 1, 2, 3, 7, being the printed labels. Seven: is 4 and 7 a second keypad entry? Eight: does any instruction depend on the display value? It read 6 last round and 2 now. Blind will report to you by voice; whatever is vital, echo it to me in gestures and I will speak it to Blind. If I misread any part of your stream, resend just that part.

Deaf's decode was nearly perfect — the only snag is that Deaf read my 🖐 wires-marker as a keypad digit "5". My format was: module hand, then that module's answer. After the keypad marker 🤟 I sent exactly one digit (✌ = press printed 2), and the 🖐 that followed was the next module marker (wires), never a digit. Likewise the "4 and 7" at the end: 4 was the keypad marker, 7 was the digit. So the true sequence, which answers all eight questions: the first action is a wire cut (1: 👎), the yellow wire 2 is cut early (2: 👍), the orange wire 1 is cut early (3: 👍), yellow comes before orange (4: 👍), "2 and 5" were not button anything — 5 was my wires marker (5: 👎), the two printed labels to enter are 2 then 7 (6: ✌ 🤞), there is a second keypad entry and its digit is 7 (7: 👍), and nothing in my manual depends on the display, the light, or the strip — all three are no-ops to me, whatever the display reads (8: 👎). The display's slide from 6 to 2 smells like a countdown, so I am resending the full four-step plan in execution order with 🤌 as a separator between modules so no digit can be mistaken for a marker, and I am closing with a lone 👍: once Deaf has relayed a step to Blind, Blind may act — no further round-trip needed. Blind's strip warning is moot: my manual never mentions the strip.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👍", "👍", "👍", "👎", "✌", "🤞", "👍", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐", "👎", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "🤌", "🤟", "✌", "🤌", "🖐", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "🤌", "🤟", "🤞"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, status from the hands. I have touched nothing and will touch nothing until the deaf one's spoken word confirmed. I hear the deaf one directly, so orders reach me the moment they are spoken. Now the urgent part: this bomb drifts. Between rounds, with nobody touching it, the display changed from six to two and the light changed from green to blue. So any manual rule keyed to the display number or the light colour cannot be judged from an old reading. Please phrase every rule as a condition: when the display shows this and the light shows that, then do this. The deaf one must re-read display and light at the moment of each action and speak the reading together with the order, and I will act on that instant pairing only. What I still need as explicit orders: the two digit keypad code, remembering the slots print two three seven one; anything the strip demands, minding the trap that its first two marks are the same shape under different colours, red then blue, with the odd third mark yellow; and the wire rules by colour and position, one orange, two yellow, three blue, four red, five white, six green. My only possible actions are pressing keypad slots one to four and cutting wire positions one to six, so nothing else can be demanded of me. The deaf one caught a contradiction in your signs and is re-confirming with you; expect more gestures and answer exactly. Last favour: gloss my gestures to the deaf one, because the deaf one misread my last trio as a number code. My signs are natural, not coded. Thumbs up means yes or understood. Thumbs down means no. The call-me hand means keep your voice coming. Raised palm means hold or waiting. The wave means hello or attention.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — I read your eight answers as: one, the first action is not a keypad entry. Two, cutting the yellow wire is an early action. Three, cutting the orange wire too. Four, yellow comes before orange. Five, two and five are not button positions. Six, the entry involves the printed digits 2 and 7. Seven, 4 and 7 are a second keypad entry. Eight, nothing depends on the display. Your longer stream I read as: cut the yellow wire, then an entry block reading 4 then 2, then cut the orange wire, then an entry block reading 4 then 7. Conflict: your answer six said the entry is 2 then 7, but the stream block says 4 then 2. Resolve it with runs of 👍 and 👎, one per question, in this exact order. One: is the full sequence cut yellow, enter a code, cut orange, enter a code? Two: is the first code, pressed by printed labels, 2 then 7? Three: is the first code instead pressed by button positions, position 4 then position 2, meaning the buttons labeled 1 then 3? Four: will the keypad's printed labels or buttons change after a wire is cut? Five: does 🤌 mean press or enter? Six: does 🤌 mean check or look? Seven: after both cuts and both entries, is the bomb defused with no further step? Eight: does the manual mention any time limit or countdown? Nine: does the manual use the light's colour or the painted strip anywhere? Then, most important: resend the two codes as number signs only, up to eight signs, nothing else before or after them. First code's two digits, then the second code's two digits. For a digit that means the printed label, send its plain number sign: ☝ one, ✌ two, 👌 three, 🤞 seven. For a digit that means a button by position from the left, send ✋ first, then the position number. So labels 2 then 7 is ✌ 🤞, and positions 4 then 2 is ✋ 🤟 ✋ ✌. If a code will only be known after a cut changes the keypad, send 👎 👎 for that code.
Deaf says: Both of you — status: sequence is cut yellow, enter a code, cut orange, enter a second code; yellow wire first is triple-confirmed. Only the code digits remain unclear. Nobody acts until I say the word CONFIRMED.

Deaf's "4 then 2" was my own fault: 🤟 is finger-code four, but I was using it as the *keypad module marker*, never a digit, and 🤌 was a mere separator between blocks. Stripping markers, my plan has exactly two keypad presses in the whole bomb. The keypad wants two digits total — and the manual's order fills them one at a time: after cutting yellow, press the key printed 2 (pad then holds one digit and waits); then cut orange; then press the key printed 7, which completes the code. The digits must **never** be entered together as "27" right after the yellow cut — that would submit the code before the orange cut and violate "in that order, and in no other."

So my nine answers: (1) the skeleton cut/enter/cut/enter is right — 👍. (2) "2 then 7" is **not** the first code — the first entry is the single digit 2 — 👎. (3) not positions 4-2 — 👎. (4) my manual says nothing about labels changing; Deaf should still re-read the keypad at the moment of each press — 👎. (5,6) 🤌 means neither press nor check; it was a separator, now abandoned — 👎👎. (7) the manual has exactly four steps and nothing after the final press — 👍. (8) no time limit or countdown in the manual — 👎. (9) the light and the strip appear nowhere — 👎.

Then the codes, pure number signs as demanded, two signs only: first entry's digit ✌ (printed 2), second entry's digit 🤞 (printed 7) — one press each, split around the orange cut. Deaf's positional framing ("first code's digits, then second code's digits") makes a two-sign stream read as one digit per code, and my 👎 on question two kills the dangerous "27 at once" parse. If Deaf still reads it differently, nobody acts until CONFIRMED, so the echo next round lets me correct it before any hand moves.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👍", "👎", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤞"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, relay this to the deaf one by gesture, it is urgent protocol. The deaf one keeps embedding gesture symbols in messages to me, but every symbol arrives to me as a blank, so I cannot see which signs were requested. From now on the deaf one should expect only these four signs from my hands: thumbs up means yes or action finished; thumbs down means no; the call-me hand means repeat your last order; raised palm means holding position. This round I answered the deaf one's four questions in order: thumbs down, no timer sounds, no ticking, beeping, humming or warmth of note; thumbs up, yes, I feel raised digits on all four keypad keys, two three seven one, so I can find any key by touch alone; thumbs up, yes, the six wires are clearly separated and I can cut one without touching its neighbours; thumbs up, yes, I can hold a finger on the yellow wire, position two, and raised palm to show I am holding ready, though note my hands reset between rounds, so the true guarantee is that the cut lands the instant the deaf one speaks the word confirmed. For your manual: the display readings so far are six, then two, changing between rounds with nobody touching the bomb. If the manual says anything about a changing display or a countdown, that pattern matters, so please check and tell the deaf one to read the display aloud to me at the moment of every action. The plan as the deaf one stated it: cut yellow position two, enter first code, cut orange position one, enter second code. I still need those code digits confirmed. I touch nothing until the deaf one says confirmed.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — your nine answers received: sequence is cut yellow, enter a code, cut orange, enter a second code, then defused. No timer, no display dependence, no light or strip use, keypad unchanged by cuts. But you answered no to the first code being labels 2 then 7, and then resended 2 then 7, which in my format means exactly that. I believe this resolves as: the first code is 7 then 2, and your 2 then 7 resend was the second code, or the set of digits used. Verify with eight thumbs in order. One: is the first code, by printed labels, 7 then 2? Two: is the second code, by printed labels, 2 then 7? Three: are the two codes different from each other? Four: does each entry use exactly two presses? Five: in your earlier long stream, did your four-sign mean the keypad module, as in my part numbering, rather than the digit four? Six: is there any special condition on the entries I have not asked about, such as holding a button, pacing between presses, or anything entered before the first cut? Seven: after cutting the yellow wire, must the code be entered immediately, or can hands move away and re-find the buttons? Eight: is it certain that nothing must be entered before the first cut? Then resend both codes in a self-checking format: each digit doubled. First code's first digit twice, first code's second digit twice, then second code's first digit twice, second code's second digit twice. Eight number signs in total, nothing else. So if the codes were 7 then 2 and 2 then 7, you would send seven, seven, two, two, two, two, seven, seven.
Deaf says: Both — one final verification round is running. Yellow cut first remains certain. Expect CONFIRMED with the full script next round. Until my voice says CONFIRMED, nothing is cut and nothing is pressed.

The loop is now precise: Deaf still models two two-press codes, and my plain "✌ 🤞" resend feeds that model every time. My manual has no codes at all — it has four steps, each keypad step a **single press**: press the key wearing 2 after the yellow cut, press the key wearing 7 after the orange cut. The pad wants two digits, so it must simply hold the first digit while the orange cut happens; the two presses together complete it. So: Q1 no (not 7-2), Q2 no (not 2-7), Q3 yes (the two entries differ — 2 then 7), **Q4 no — the heart of it: one press per entry**, Q5 yes (🤟 was the keypad module marker), Q6 no special conditions, Q7 no immediacy demanded (only order matters — hands may move away between steps), Q8 yes, certainly nothing before the first cut, since the yellow cut *is* step one.

For the eight-sign self-check I keep Deaf's doubling but use the nulls Deaf themselves established (👎👎 = "no such thing," as in "no code known"): ✌✌ then 👎👎 — first entry is the single digit 2, there is no second digit; 🤞🤞 then 👎👎 — second entry is the single digit 7, no second digit. Read together with the 👎 on Q4, this can only resolve as cut yellow, press 2, cut orange, press 7. I also glossed Blind's gesture code for my own part: last round Blind sent 👍 🤙 ✋ = "yes / repeat your last order / holding" — Deaf saw the same trio and should read it as Blind's protocol, not as numbers.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎", "👍", "👎", "👍", "👎", "👎", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌", "👎", "👎", "🤞", "🤞", "👎", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, relay to the deaf one. My three answer signs in order were thumbs up, wave, thumbs up, then a final raised palm. One: thumbs up, yes, I understood, I will go by positions, second wire from the left for yellow, leftmost for orange. Two: the wave is a no, and here is the truth it carries: I have never pressed a keypad key, so I cannot yet promise I feel a press register. The first press is the test. If the manual allows a pause between the two code digits, the safe protocol is: I press digit one, then sign thumbs up if it visibly clicked or sank, wave if I felt nothing, and only then continue. If the manual demands the digits back to back, I will enter them in one motion and report feedback after. Please check which the manual allows and tell the deaf one. Three: thumbs up, yes, I can cut the yellow wire, position two, in one clean motion without touching positions one or three. Four: the raised palm is what my earlier open hand always meant, it is the holding sign from the four-sign vocabulary I sent you last round: thumbs up yes or finished, thumbs down no, call-me hand repeat the order, raised palm holding ready. Please make sure the deaf one has that list. Two cautions for your manual check. First, my hands reset between rounds, so holding means readiness; the guarantee is that the cut lands the instant the deaf one says confirmed. Second, the bomb drifts: display went six then two, light went green then blue. Please confirm the plan, cut yellow position two first, then code, then cut orange position one, then second code, works no matter what the display or light currently shows. If any rule references them, the deaf one must read them aloud at the moment of each action. Last: please double check the code digits against the button map, slots print two three seven one, left to right. I have still touched nothing.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute — new reading, verify hard. I believe each entry is ONE press, not two: entry A is pressing the button labeled 2, the leftmost button, after the yellow cut; entry B is pressing the button labeled 7, the third button, after the orange cut. Your resend then meant: digit 2 with no second digit, digit 7 with no second digit. Answer with exactly eight thumbs in order, yes or no. One: is entry A a single press of the leftmost button, the one labeled 2? Two: is entry B a single press of the third button, the one labeled 7? Three: in your resend, did each thumbs-down pair mean no second digit exists? Four: is the full sequence cut yellow, press 2 once, cut orange, press 7 once, then defused? Five: does nothing on the bomb's display, light, or strip matter at any step? Six: must each press come immediately after its cut, hands not wandering? Seven: after the press of 7, is everything finished? Eight: is there truly nothing entered, cut or pressed before the yellow cut? If every answer is yes, send eight thumbs-up and nothing else, and my voice next round runs the whole script. If ANY answer is no, send its question number as a number sign first, then thumbs for your correction — for example, if question two is wrong, send ✌ then the corrected facts as number signs.
